Three of the most closely watched names in AI-era software are trading lower after a rough session. CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) trades at $231.84, Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) at $146.07 and Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) at $278.94.

Thinkstock

Today they're down 4.77%, 4.95% and 8.15%, respectively. If you split $7,500 evenly, each stock gets a $2,500 stake. All three just reported record quarters, so it's fair to ask whether this basket can double to $15,000 by 2030.

Base Case: $7,500 Could Grow to About $13,805.50

Our model projects prices one year and five years out. The 2030 target falls between those two, so the figures below use the five-year window that ends in November 2031.

In the base case, a $7,500 investment could be worth about $13,805.50, a total return of 84.0733%. Only the bull case gets past $15,000, reaching $15,649 (108.6533%). In the bear case, the basket ends at $8,635.75 (15.1433%).

Those totals rest on five-year base-case targets of $393.17 for CrowdStrike, $281.22 for Palantir and $596.23 for Cloudflare. Returns start from the model's reference prices: $242.37, $146.07 and $301.93.

For November 2030 alone, the base-case path passes through $372.83, $267.93 and $559.66. Those 2030 numbers are rough waypoints on the five-year path.

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Zscaler (ZS) stock fell 18.1% over the month to November 20, 2026, against a 9.7% fall for the S&P 500. Holders may see that as a pause in a business that is still growing fast. That view holds only if Zscaler made back its past market falls within months and keeps its sales growing. So how much did Zscaler holders lose the last times the market turned, and how long did they wait?

How Far Has Zscaler Stock Fallen In Market Shocks?

Zscaler stock lost 57.7% in the worst of its seven market shocks, while the S&P 500 lost 24.0%. That fall came in 2022, during the inflation shock and Fed tightening. Across all seven shocks, Zscaler fell 28.0% on average, against 17.1% for the index. So the stock has usually fallen further than the market.

Zscaler stock lost 57.7% of its value in the 2022 market shock. If much of your savings sits in this one stock, a drop like that is hard to sit through, and getting out can cost you in taxes. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

The 2023 SVB banking crisis showed the same pattern. Zscaler fell 35.0% then, while the S&P 500 fell only 6.7%.

Most of those falls were made back within months, but not the deepest one. The median wait from the low back to the old peak was 1.1 months. After its May 2022 low, Zscaler took 36.4 months to get back to its January 2022 peak, in June 2025. All seven falls have since been made back. Measured from its November 2021 high to its May 2023 low, though, the stock fell 76.4%.

Zscaler's Sales Kept Growing In Fiscal 2026

Zscaler's sales growth held up in fiscal 2026, the year to July 31, 2026. Revenue reached $3,353 million, up 25.4% from a year earlier. That picked up from 23.3% growth in fiscal 2025, though growth ran at 34.1% in fiscal 2024. Part of the gain came from Red Canary, a business Zscaler bought. Excluding it, revenue grew 20%, management said on the September 3, 2026 call. That was slower than in fiscal 2025.

Zscaler still loses money on its operations, but far less than it did. Its operating loss was 3.6% of revenue in fiscal 2026, against 30.9% in fiscal 2021. The company also held $3,474 million in cash and short-term investments at July 31, 2026. That compares with $1,856 million of debt.

Management Expects Zscaler's Growth To Slow In Fiscal 2027

On September 3, 2026, management guided fiscal 2027 revenue to $3,908 million to $3,938 million. Management put that at growth of 16.6% to 17.5% from a year earlier.

Key Takeaways

Zscaler jumped 23% after CrowdStrike agreed to buy it in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion.

CrowdStrike's drop shrank the offer's value, and Zscaler trades just below it.

Investors expect the deal to close, near analysts' average target.

Palo Alto Networks and Cloudflare now face a much bigger zero-trust rival.

Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ) shares are up 23% today after CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) agreed to buy it in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion.

Bloomberg reported the talks after Friday's close, and the companies confirmed it before Monday's open. "Today, safety is required to let AI in," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in its release.

It also hands Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) and Cloudflare (NET:NYSE), which compete with Zscaler for zero-trust customers, a much bigger rival.

Zscaler sells after a strong quarter

Zscaler's fiscal first quarter, reported with the deal, was strong: revenue rose 20% to $949.3 million, and ARR grew 21% to $3.88 billion. Analysts expected normalized EPS to rise from $4.21 in fiscal 2026 to $5.63 in fiscal 2028:

Zscaler (ZS): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to July) (TIKR)

At the announced price, CrowdStrike is paying about 53x forward earnings, up from about 40x at Friday's close.

TIKR tracks 47 analysts on Zscaler. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Zscaler, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Zscaler's Analyst Ratings

The premium shrank overnight

Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares apiece, which the companies valued at $260.41 a share at Friday's close, a 34% premium. But CrowdStrike fell 5% after hours on the report. That takes the offer to roughly $238, and today's jump leaves Zscaler just a few percent below it.

That's close to where analysts already had the stock, with an average price target of $236 on Friday:

Zscaler (ZS): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
A bigger rival for Palo Alto and Cloudflare

CrowdStrike is buying its way to the kind of broad platform Palo Alto has bet customers want. Palo Alto's fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 39% to $3.44 billion, with help from its CyberArk purchase, and it raised its full-year outlook. Cloudflare's third-quarter revenue also rose 39%, to $782.5 million, and it's now one of the few independent zero-trust players left. Both could pick up customers who'd rather wait out a long integration.

A fair price, paid in a falling stock

Zscaler holders are getting a fair, if hardly generous, exit: about the Street's own target, after a quarter of 20% growth. I read the tight gap as the market expecting the deal to close as planned, in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028). If Zscaler's discount widens well past a few percent, investors are starting to doubt regulators will sign off.

Zscaler traded about 16% above Friday's close, a move that also follows the late-Friday report of CrowdStrike talks. The figures below explain Friday's fall and are at Friday's close.

Zscaler (ZS) stock fell 5.3% on Friday, November 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 3.7%. The company had no earnings report or SEC filing around the move. Late on November 20, CrowdStrike was said to be in talks to buy Zscaler, and Zscaler stock jumped 20% on that report. The 5.3% fall is measured at Friday's close, before that jump. Technology stocks fell harder still that day. XLK, the fund that tracks the technology sector, dropped 7.3%. So what ties Zscaler to a day when technology stocks sold off?

Zscaler lost 5.3% in a single session with no earnings report behind it. If a big part of your savings sits in this one stock, a bad day for technology stocks becomes a bad day for you. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

How Zscaler's Growth Is Tied To AI

Technology stocks sold off hard on November 20. Anthropic, a maker of AI models, began trading the day before in the biggest IPO in history. Its shares dropped as the rout deepened. The selloff had grown worse through the week, and the S&P 500 was heading for its longest losing streak since 2020.

Zscaler sits close to that AI story. On its September 3, 2026 call, management said AI was quickly becoming the largest tailwind the company had ever seen. That demand shows up in Zscaler's data security and security for AI products. Bookings for security for AI rose more than 50% in fiscal Q4 2026 from the quarter before. On November 20, Zscaler also announced partnerships with Anthropic and Mistral to help companies use AI safely. So by management's own account, a Zscaler holder owns a business whose growth now rises with AI.

Did Zscaler Fall Alone That Day?

No. Its sub-industry, systems software, has 29 other companies worth $2 billion or more. Of those, 27 fell and only 2 rose. Their median fall was 3.7%, against Zscaler's 5.3%. And 11 of them fell 5% or more. All five companies on Zscaler's peer list fell too, from Netskope's 3.5% to Cloudflare's 9.5%. So Zscaler fell with its group, a bit more than the typical systems software stock but less than XLK.

Here is What to Know Beyond Why Cloudflare, Inc. (NET) is a Trending Stock

Cloudflare (NET) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this web security and content delivery company have returned 0%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -6.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Cloudflare falls in, has lost 13.3%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Cloudflare is expected to post earnings of $0.42 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +50%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +60.5%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.34 points to a change of +44.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +40.5%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.86 indicates a change of +38.8% from what Cloudflare is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +8.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Cloudflare.
